events.title: Operation Dynamo Begins
events.description: The British evacuation of Allied troops from the beaches and harbor of Dunkirk, France, began after German forces had trapped the British Expeditionary Force and French units. Over nine days, more than 330,000 soldiers were rescued by naval vessels and civilian boats.
events.significance: The evacuation preserved the core of the British Army, allowing Britain to continue fighting in World War II, and became a symbol of resilience, known as the 'Dunkirk spirit'.

events.title: Impeachment Trial of Andrew Johnson Ends
events.description: The U.S. Senate voted to acquit President Andrew Johnson on the remaining impeachment articles, after the earlier May 16 vote, and ended the trial. The case stemmed from his violation of the Tenure of Office Act by attempting to remove Secretary of War Edwin Stanton. The Senate fell one vote short of the two-thirds majority needed for conviction.
events.significance: The acquittal set an important precedent protecting the presidency from removal over political disagreements and shaped the balance of power between Congress and the executive branch.

events.title: Apollo 10 Returns to Earth
events.description: Apollo 10 astronauts Thomas Stafford, John Young, and Eugene Cernan splashed down in the Pacific Ocean after an eight-day mission that orbited the Moon. The crew conducted a full dress rehearsal for the lunar landing, with the lunar module descending to within about 15 kilometers of the surface.
events.significance: The mission tested all the procedures and hardware for a lunar landing except the landing itself, paving the way for Apollo 11 to land humans on the Moon two months later.

events.title: Guyana Gains Independence
events.description: British Guiana became the independent nation of Guyana, ending decades of British colonial rule on the northeastern coast of South America. Forbes Burnham later led the country as it developed its own government.
events.significance: Guyana's independence was part of the broader post-war wave of decolonization and created the only English-speaking nation in South America.

events.title: Dracula Is Published
events.description: Bram Stoker's Gothic horror novel Dracula was published in London by Archibald Constable and Company. The epistolary novel introduced Count Dracula and drew on folklore about vampires.
events.significance: Dracula became one of the most influential works of horror fiction, shaping the modern vampire archetype in literature, film, and popular culture.
